steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil; stir in tortellini and return to a boil. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tortellini float to the top and the filling is hot, about 3 minutes, or according to package directions. Drain, rinse with cold water, and refrigerate until cool, about 30 minutes.

Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate; drain. Chop into ½-inch pieces while still a little warm.
Combine tortellini, bacon, broccoli, grape tomatoes, and green onions in a bowl; pour dressing over top and toss lightly to coat. Chill in the refrigerator before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Tortellini Bacon Broccoli Salad
raw_recipe.description: This pasta salad recipe is made with cheese tortellini, bacon, and broccoli with a coleslaw dressing. It makes a flavorful side, lunch, or light meal.

review.reviewBody: A friend and I followed this recipe almost exactly (we doubled the green onion because we love them) and it was SO good! We were a bit skeptical about the coleslaw dressing but it added a wonderful touch of sweetness to the ingredients. The salad was even better the 2nd day so I'd recommend making it the night before if possible to allow the flavors to meld together... YUMMY! Thanks for sharing!

This was even better than reviewers said! The ingredients all complement each other so nicely. I was very skeptical at the cole slaw dressing but it was the best! I used Marie's Cole Slaw dressing usually found in the dairy section in the fresh produce section in the grocery store. I didn't have any onion but that's the only change I made. I cut the recipe in half for just the two of us and wish I had made the full recipe. My husband asked for seconds. That NEVER happens. The downside of this recipe is the number of carbs in it so it will only be a once-in-a-while treat for us, or for when company comes, or for when I have to bring something to a potluck, or when I'm in a bad mood, or when I'm in a good mood. Love this stuff! 

I forgot to add that I added my broccoli into the tortellini about five minutes before the tortellini finished cooking. Not a fan of raw broccoli!

I’ve made this recipe several times. I usually double the amount of coleslaw dressing and add some garlic salt, celery salt, pepper, and celery seed. I make the tortellini the night before and use a cup of the dressing and let it soak overnight then add the other ingredients in the morning. I have also replaced the broccoli with romaine lettuce before and its great that way too!

My favorite broccoli salad. But I did tweak it a little bit. I blanch the broccoli by throwing it into the water with the tortellini for one minute (when the tortellini is almost done) and then drain tortellini and broccoli together, and rinse under cold water to cool. I add 1 large stalk of celery, finely diced. I use a thick sliced applewood bacon for this recipe, and cut into 3/4 inch pieces. For the dressing, after frying the bacon and draining off the grease, I add a little bit of water (3 tbsp?) to deglaze the bacon pan, and stir to scrape up all the tasty bits. To this I add 1/2 tbsp. horseradish and a scant 1/4 c of bottled poppyseed dressing. This salad is a flavor explosion.

This is delicious!! I used a bunch of green onions because I love them and two didn’t seem like enough, chopped the bacon before cooking it, and blanched the broccoli before cutting it up. I also made my own favorite coleslaw dressing: 2/3 cup mayonnaise, 3 Tbsp vegetable oil, 1 Tbsp white vinegar, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp poppy seeds. It hasn’t even been thoroughly refrigerated yet but I tasted it and I didn’t want to stop eating it!!!

I made this before and enjoyed it. I didn't get much of a reaction from anyone so I forgot about it. Recently I needed an easy side to pair with broiled garlic chicken thighs. I made this recipe but used more chives and added diced red onion. I threw the fresh broccoli in with the boiling pasta for the last forty-five seconds to make it more tender. I used Marie's cole slaw dressing and let it sit in the fridge for a few hours. Also, I chopped the bacon before I fried it. I've read that it's better the next day but I wouldn't know. I doubled the recipe for twelve people and they ate it all (almost all, someone took the little that was left home). Several people asked me for the recipe, I even got a text the next day. This went right into the favorite list. I have a barbecue this weekend with a different group of people and plan to make it again. Easily five stars!

I used about 3/4 c sunflower seeds and half a jar of dressing. 1/2 lb turkey bacon and 1/2 lb reg bacon. 1 lb cooked seasoned chicken breast cut in cubes. Blanched broccoli in pasta water. Let it sit over nite in refrigerator.

I just made a half sized batch of this to test it before a ladies lunch, and it got huge "thumbs up" reviews in our house! I improvised on the dressing because I didn't have any, nor the ingredients to make it, so I doctored up bottled ranch (about 3/4 c) with a splash of cider vinegar, about 2 T sugar, and about two t. poppy seeds. Worked great! I look forward to making this often in the future using the coleslaw dressing and maybe switching up the pasta. Thanks for sharing! UPDATE (5/19/14) I have made this several times since my last review, and it's made even better with tiny cubes of cheddar thrown in, about 2 oz worth. It's a bit finicky to cut the cubes, but my husband thought I'd bought it from a caterer the first time I made it this way, which I guess is a good thing. UPDATE (AGAIN)4/9/15: if your crowd doesn't like onions (my hubs HATES them raw), try mixing in large chunks of red onion, then selecting around them when you serve. The onion flavor is still there, but the haters won't crunch down on an unwelcome surprise. LOVE this salad, as it's an especially good way to use the broccoli stalks (sliced thinly and par-cooked and shocked), so they don't go to waste.

This was wonderful! Don't let the coleslaw dressing fool you. I bought Marzetti's refrigerated dressing. I cooked the bacon in the microwave. I did blanch the broccoli as others suggested. I also added fresh mozzarella cheese. My family loved it.

Not re-inventing the wheel here. These are all ingredients I like and use regularly. I had never used "Coleslaw Dressing" before, but I bought a bottle. Then, when I got home I noticed the first ingredient is High Fructose Corn Syrup...so I made a Lite Mayo, garlic, Dijon dressing instead. I also blanched the Broccoli since I'm not a big fan of the raw version. This all came out quite nice. Good and flexible recipe.

Made this exactly as written and it deserves all 5 stars. I used Marie's coleslaw dressing which is excellent. Made it again tonight as a main meal with the addition of 12 ounces of ham and served it with crusty french rolls.
I first made this for my niece's bridal shower and several people asked for the recipe. It has since become a family favorite. Delicious!!

I made the recipe as written with gluten free pasta (I think it was tortelloni instead of tortellini if we want to be picky). The flavor of the recipe highly depends on the coleslaw dressing you use. My pasta salad was a bit underwhelming and was on the blander side and I thought it could use a bit more dressing. It could definitely use some tweaks or a more flavorful dressing.

This was good as made to the recipe, but it needed more flavor to me. I par cooked the broccoli with the fresh tortellini because we don't like it raw. Next time I would add some fresh cracked pepper, oregano, garlic powder and possibly some cheese.

Boring, needs Flavor. I made it according to the recipe and now I have doctor it up. so I can eat it considering I have a giant bowlful. They forgot flavor. One dimension of flavor. ZZZZZZZ! It's a real bummer when you spend money on the ingredients, take the time to make it and it's so incredibly boring. If you make it immediately plan on adding some flavor dimensions from the start.
The first time I made this was for a potluck and it was a big hit with everyone. Have made it many times since, one of my go to recipes for summer.
Every time I make this salad for a dinmer everyone wants the recipe. It is a favorite with my family as well.

It was awesome but, as everyone else made some changes. Instead of green onion I used chopped red onion. I also added shredded mozzarella, quartered pepperoni slices. I used a little more broccoli and a tad more dressing. It was absolutely amazing!

This is AMAZINGLY yummy! And very easy to make. It's my go-to salad in the summer and I always get asked for the recipe. I use real bacon crumbles (ala Costco) to substitute for having to cook the bacon - so much easier, and the results are great. Sometimes I add chopped red pepper or shredded cheddar just to mix it up, but it's wonderful as written too!

I wanted to make a filling summer salad. This fit the bill. I was out of broccoli, so I used fresh green pepper, red onion, and carrots instead. I didn’t have store-made coleslaw dressing, so I made my own version with mayo, plain Greek yogurt, and some lemon white balsamic vinegar. I served with with a “regular” salad. Perfect summer dinner.
